changelog:
**Prefer original audio (VO)** now finds the original track even when nothing in the file says
which one it is. If you have that option switched on, read the upgrade note — this one can
change which audio track you get.

## ✨ Changed

- **The original version is found from the item's metadata when no track is tagged.** Until now
  the option read the track *title* and nothing else, looking for `Original`, `VO` or
  `Version Originale`. On a release that labels its tracks that works. On one shipping a dozen
  untitled dubs it matched nothing, said nothing, and quietly handed the decision back to your
  priority list — which is the opposite of what the option promises.

  Three signals are now tried, most trustworthy first:

  1. the container's `original` flag, when the release set it;
  2. an `Original` / `VO` / `Version Originale` keyword in the track title — the previous
     behaviour, unchanged, and still what serves releases labelling VO and VF;
  3. failing both, the original language recorded in the item's own metadata, inherited from
     the series for an episode, matched against each track's language tag. Metadata saying
     `de` finds a track tagged `ger`.

  A worked example: a German film also carrying Chinese, English and Japanese audio, for a
  viewer whose audio list runs *Chinese > Korean > Japanese > English > French*. It used to
  play in **Chinese** — German is not on the list, so it could not win, and the option had no
  way to say "the original, whatever language that is". It now plays in **German**.

- **The log says which signal found the track.** `(via container flag)`, `(via track title)` or
  `(via original language de)`. "Why did it pick that track" is where every report starts.

## ⬆️ Upgrading

**This can change the audio track you get.** The original version now wins even when its
language appears on neither of your lists — that is the point of the option, and it is
something an ordered list of languages cannot express on its own. If you had *Prefer original
audio (VO)* switched on without it ever appearing to do anything, it will start doing
something. Switch it off if you would rather your priority list stayed in charge.

Nothing else changes: subtitle selection, series overrides and both language lists behave
exactly as in 1.3.2.0. Server compatibility is unchanged (**Jellyfin 12.x**); 10.11 servers
stay on 1.2.0.1.

## 🔧 Under the hood

- The metadata lookup is the last branch, so it never runs for a file that identified itself,
  and costs a property read when it does — the parent walk for an episode reaches a series the
  handler has already resolved for series overrides.
- Workflow maintenance: the GitHub actions move to their current majors, which run on Node 24
  instead of the deprecated Node 20, the config page tests run on Node 24, and the runner image
  is pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` rather than following `ubuntu-latest` onto Ubuntu 26 unannounced.
description: Per-user audio and subtitle language priority with fallback. Automatically selects the best audio and subtitle tracks based on an ordered language preference list, with per-series overrides.
